# Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash GA，Anthropic 公开 dreaming

今日要点

- Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 进入 GA，720p 价格降 30%
- Anthropic 公开 Claude dreaming 机制，后台整理记忆并纠错
- DeepMind AI 智能体发现旧版 1024 位 RSA 两处弱点

上一期 · 2026-11-06 已是最新一期
 Google DeepMind 将 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 推向 GA，720p 价格 $0.07/秒、较 1.1 降 30%；Anthropic 公开 Claude dreaming 机制，后台整理记忆并纠错；DeepMind 称 AI 智能体发现旧版 1024 位 RSA 两处弱点。  

### 1️⃣ OpenRouter 发布 Auto Code 与新一代 Auto Router#

- 发布：OpenRouter 推出面向通用问答与 Agent 的 Auto Router，以及面向编码 Agent 的 Auto Code。官方称 Auto Code 基准接近 Opus 5.5，成本低 74%，p90 延迟 0.65 秒。
- 内测数据：无效工具调用降 4 倍，Agent 响应截断减半，延迟降 3 倍；每次请求的路由决策可查看。
- 行业意义：模型路由从“自动选模型”细分为按任务类型、成本与延迟约束调度，成为多模型应用的成本控制层。 🔗 OpenRouter 发布 | 内测数据 | 官方博客

### 2️⃣ Google DeepMind：AI 智能体发现旧版 1024 位 RSA 两处弱点#

- 研究结果：Google DeepMind 公布，在人类引导下，AI 智能体发现旧版 1024 位 RSA 密码系统的两处重大弱点；现代 2048 位系统不受这些特定 exploit 影响。
- 方法：研究用 AI agents 加速密码学压力测试，探索历史安全假设之外的攻击面。
- 行业意义：AI 被用于密码分析与安全审计，密码标准需要持续压测；DeepMind 明确提醒，不能把历史安全性假设当作静态结论。 🔗 DeepMind 公告 | 后续说明 | 研究文章

### 3️⃣ Meta 将 Muse Wonder 专用模型接入 Muse 与 Meta AI#

- 发布：Meta 将使用 Muse Wonder 训练的专用模型接入 Muse 与 Meta AI，包含 Active Memory 与 Active Focus。
- 指标：在 Muse 中，关键目标信息遗忘减少 2.4 倍，约束变化时“脱困”能力提升 67%；Meta AI 可分解复杂问题、追问并适应方向变化。
- 行业意义：助手从单轮回答转向在任务推进中维护目标状态、区分过时信息，并在约束变化时重规划。 🔗 Meta 公告 | 研究博客

### 4️⃣ Notion 发布 ChatGPT 插件，工作区进入对话界面#

- 产品：Notion 发布 ChatGPT 插件，用户可在对话内使用真实 Notion 编辑器创建页面、边聊边改，也可自己接管编辑。
- 双向集成：Notion 侧可用 OpenAI 模型，ChatGPT 侧通过 MCP 调用 Notion，并支持用 ChatGPT 订阅使用 Notion；Notion 称正推进其他模型提供商。
- 行业意义：工作区与对话界面开始双向嵌入，插件与 MCP 成为 SaaS 在 Agent 入口中的分发方式。 🔗 Notion 发布 | Notion CEO 说明 | 插件入口

### 5️⃣ AWS SageMaker Inference 支持 MIG GPU 分区#

- 发布：Amazon SageMaker Inference 支持 NVIDIA MIG GPU 分区，单卡可切成最多 7 个硬件隔离分区，每个分区部署不同模型。
- 实测：H100 的 mig-3g.40gb 分区对比整卡 A100-40GB，输出吞吐高 53%–89%，token 间延迟低 8.9%–42.1%，每百万输出 token 成本低 18%–34%，主要在高并发长上下文场景。
- 限制：需使用 inference components；布局在创建端点时固定，变更需新端点与流量迁移；不支持 serverless 与异步推理。
- 行业意义：推理成本优化从“整卡租用”转向按模型需求切片，提升小模型、多租户和流水线部署的 GPU 利用率。 🔗 AWS 博客

### 6️⃣ GitHub 披露 Agentic 工程规模数据与并发 Git 存储架构#

- 规模数据：GitHub 称 2026 年 10 月一周提交量超过 12 亿次，同比增长 400%+；Faros AI 研究显示，团队从低 AI 采用升至高采用后，PR 在审查阶段停留时间增加 441%。
- 工作流：GitHub 提出 Plan/Build/Verify/Observe 的 agentic engineering 流程，包括栈式 PR、Copilot 代码审查、Agent Merge 自动处理失败检查与合并冲突。
- 基础设施：GitHub 新 Git 存储架构内部测试支持 5000 个并发 Agent 操作同一仓库，每秒 7200 次 push，同时维持读延迟。
- 行业意义：代码生成量上升后，评审队列与并发版本库操作成为新的瓶颈，工具链需要围绕 Agent 并发重做。 🔗 GitHub 博客 | 存储架构测试

### 7️⃣ Anthropic：Claude 用“dreaming”整理 Agent 记忆#

- 机制：Anthropic 工程博客介绍 Claude 的“dreaming”机制：在后台整理已学到的记忆、纠正错误，并在后续任务中更快检索所需信息。
- 定位：记忆被视为 Claude 从经验中学习的关键组件，不只是对话历史缓存；工程博客拆解了 Agent 记忆的组成部分。
- 行业意义：Agent 记忆从“检索外挂”走向后台整理、压缩与纠错，记忆质量开始成为长任务稳定性的工程指标。 🔗 Anthropic 公告 | 工程博客

### 8️⃣ [持续跟踪] 企业 token 支出增速停滞，Anthropic IPO 估值预期继续下修#

- 前情提要：此前市场已关注 Anthropic IPO 估值预期下修，以及 AI 资本开支与收入增速是否匹配。
- 最新数据：Ramp 统计显示，8 月初至 10 月中企业 token 用量增约 65%，token 支出仅增 1.5%；OpenAI 与 Anthropic 综合单价一个月从 0.76 降至 0.56 美元/百万 token，降 27%。
- 公司侧：Anthropic 招股书显示 Q3 收入环比增 47%，但新模型降价与合同折扣抵掉约 6 亿美元收入；报道中的潜在投资者估值讨论降至 1.2 万亿至 1.3 万亿美元区间。
- 行业意义：token 用量增长与支出脱钩，价格战、模型路由和企业预算控制压缩单价；按 token 计费的模型厂商需要靠 token 效率和应用层价值维持收入增长。Ramp 样本偏科技企业，需注意代表性。 🔗 宝玉整理 | TechCrunch 报道 | Ramp 报告

# Meta ships Wonder-trained models to Muse and Meta AI users, TNS reports

The unnamed “specialized” models reach a free consumer tier and Meta AI inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, while Meta keeps the frontier Muse Wonder model itself for paying subscribers on harder tasks.

Everyone using Meta's Muse agent and its Meta AI service began receiving new models on Friday, November 6, that the company says it trained using Muse Wonder, its frontier model. The New Stack's Frederic Lardinois reported the rollout, noting that subscribers still get Wonder itself for harder tasks. Meta has not named the new models and describes them only as “specialized” versions of its existing ones.[1]

Meta launched Wonder and the more capable Wonder Full on October 12, according to the report. Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and in Muse Code, Meta's coding agent, while Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code's two most expensive plans. Muse, Meta's personal agent app, launched in September running on the smaller Muse Spark model.[1]

## Evidence

The new models carry two features Meta first introduced with Wonder. Active Memory is meant to let a model carry details from earlier conversations into new ones; Meta says it trained the models to tell temporary information from permanent and to distinguish what is still relevant from what has gone stale. On Meta's internal evaluation, the new models in Muse correctly use critical context in 90% of tasks, up from 76% for the previous model. Active Focus is aimed at keeping a model working when a task breaks down, and Meta reports a 67% improvement in finishing routine tasks that run into unexpected problems, though it did not share the baseline for that figure. Meta also says the models are better at judging when to work independently and when to check with the user, and that they handle corrections made mid-task. The company has not detailed its training method.[1]

## Why it matters

Lardinois frames the economics plainly: Wonder costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens on the API, while Muse has a free tier and Meta AI runs inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. Training lighter-weight models with Wonder, he writes, is likely cheaper than serving Wonder itself to that many users. He also notes that Muse's free tier sets a lower barrier to entry than OpenAI's Dots or Anthropic's Duet, which he reports are available only to subscribers on those vendors' highest pricing tiers.[1]

Meta.title: Dell RAG 聊天机器人蓝图验证了 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

Meta.content:
Dell RAG 聊天机器人蓝图验证了 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

关键要点

Dell 的 RAG 聊天机器人蓝图验证了 meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 是一款可在 Gaudi 硬件上用于生产环境的模型。

该架构结合了运行在 5001 端口的 FastAPI 后端、运行在 3000 端口的 React 前端、LangChain、FAISS-CPU 向量数据库和企业级推理端点。

用户通过拖放界面上传 PDF，触发文本切分、嵌入向量生成、相似度搜索，以及 LLM 基于上下文生成回复。

Dell 的 RAG Chatbot 蓝图将 meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 列为经过验证、适用于 Gaudi 硬件的模型。该蓝图介绍了一款用于基于文档进行问答的全栈检索增强生成应用，结合了基于 FastAPI 和 LangChain 的后端、FAISS 和 AI 模型，以及基于 React + Vite + Tailwind CSS 的前端。该系统支持 PDF 上传、文档处理、嵌入生成、相似度搜索，以及由大型语言模型基于上下文生成回复。

RAG Chatbot 蓝图连接文档检索与 LLM 回复

RAG Chatbot 蓝图介绍了一种可用于生产环境的架构，用于回答有关已上传文档的问题。用户通过拖放界面上传 PDF，随后后端会拆分文本、将其转换为嵌入，并将嵌入存储在 FAISS 向量数据库中。在聊天交互过程中，用户查询会触发相似度搜索，为大型语言模型提供相关上下文，以生成综合回复。

该项目可与云托管 API 或本地模型端点集成。据介绍，它适用于研究、企业和教育环境。

FastAPI 后端和 React 前端构成服务架构

该架构由运行在 3000 端口上的 React Web UI 和运行在 5001 端口上的 FastAPI 后端组成。React 界面提供 PDF 上传、实时聊天、响应式设计和实时状态更新。FastAPI 后端负责预处理、嵌入、向量存储、检索、LLM 编排、身份验证和健康检查。

后端包含由 LangChain 驱动的文档处理、用于相似度搜索的 FAISS-CPU 向量存储、用于嵌入和 LLM 的企业推理端点、推理 API 的基于令牌的身份验证、文件验证和大小限制、CORS 支持、健康检查端点，以及由路由和服务组成的模块化架构。前端支持拖放式 PDF 上传、实时聊天界面、Tailwind CSS、Vite、实时状态更新和适配移动设备的设计。

Docker Compose 部署使用企业推理端点

该蓝图要求安装 Docker 和 Docker Compose，并能够访问企业推理端点，例如支持基于令牌身份验证的 GenAI Gateway 或 APISIX Gateway。配置使用根目录下的 .env 文件设置 Docker Compose 变量，并使用 api/.env 文件配置后端应用。这些设置定义模型名称、端点 URL、令牌、SSL 设置和可选的本地域名映射。

部署时使用 docker compose up 启动 UI 和后端服务。API 可通过 http://localhost:5001 访问，UI 可通过 http://localhost:3000 访问。该蓝图还提供诊断命令和健康检查，用于验证运行状态。

对于 APISIX/Keycloak 部署，模型名称必须包含在端点 URL 中，https://apisix-gateway.example.com/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 是一个示例。嵌入服务使用单独的端点，https://apisix-gateway.example.com/bge-base-en-v1.5 是嵌入模型的一个示例。

RAG Chatbot 蓝图列出经过验证的模型和硬件

该蓝图列出了经过验证的 RAGChatbot 模型，并说明其适配的硬件平台。

meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 已通过 Gaudi 硬件验证。

BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5（嵌入）已通过 Gaudi 硬件验证。

Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct 已通过 Xeon 硬件验证。

React Web UI 运行在 3000 端口上。

FastAPI 后端运行在 5001 端口上。

该应用使用 FAISS-CPU 进行向量存储和相似度搜索。

Dell RAG Chatbot 蓝图验证了哪个 Llama 模型？

该蓝图将 meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 列为经过验证、适用于 Gaudi 硬件的模型。

RAG Chatbot 使用哪些组件进行基于文档的问答？

该系统结合了 FastAPI 后端、LangChain、FAISS、AI 模型，以及 React + Vite + Tailwind CSS 前端。它会处理上传的 PDF、创建嵌入、将嵌入存储在 FAISS 向量数据库中、检索相关上下文，并将该上下文发送给大型语言模型以生成回复。

DeepSeek Harness stated that it aims to become the operating system in the Agent era, providing users with stable basic capabilities and general functions, while professional scenarios, specific industries and personalized needs are realized by developers through plugins. Its proposed "Everything is a Plugin" design even means that built-in functions can also be replaced by third-party plugins.

Since the release of the v0.1 version on August 13, DeepSeek Harness is expanding from an Agent tool to an open application platform. Community developers have developed a large number of third-party plugins around scenarios such as content creation, design, context management and scientific research.

However, as the number of plugins increases, new problems are also emerging: the more plugins there are, does the Agent really become more capable? Will a large number of plugin descriptions and tool rules take up the model's context and increase execution costs? For ordinary users, should they be given the space for free combination capabilities, or a complete out-of-the-box product?

Highly open, but will more plugins make the Agent harder to use?

The highly open plugin architecture of DeepSeek Harness is its most attractive feature: users do not have to accept the Agent workflow predefined by the manufacturer, but can combine models, tools, memory and interfaces according to their own needs to build an exclusive working environment.

Some users shared that they previously mainly used Hermes to handle general tasks and OMP for programming, but neither of the two tools could fully meet their customization needs. Other developers have launched TheOne plugin, which identifies the topic of user messages through large language models and automatically routes them to corresponding independent sessions, avoiding mixing multiple projects and topics in the same conversation. There are also community projects that use the ESP32-S3 development board as a USB mouse and keyboard for iPhone, and receive the mobile phone screen mirroring through AirPlay at the same time. The Agent can take screenshots, click, long press, slide and enter text to control a real non-jailbroken iPhone.

The plugin ecosystem of DeepSeek Harness has seen a large number of applications with practical use value. But on the other hand, while plugins expand capabilities, they may also increase the complexity of using the Agent.

On November 5, a developer shared his experience of actively deleting plugins from "relying on plugins for everything". He said that he once installed more than 15 plugins for the Agent, but as the number of plugins increased, the system encountered problems such as infinite loops, context overflow and increased Token consumption.

In his opinion, every time a plugin is added, the model needs to additionally understand the corresponding description, usage rules and constraints. If the information of a large number of plugins enters the context at the same time, the model has to spend more attention on processing the tools themselves instead of focusing on task reasoning. This is only the experience of individual users, but it at least reflects users' attention to the cost of calling tools.

# What Is DeepSeek? The AI Lab and Its Models Explained

A plain-English guide to DeepSeek: who runs the Chinese AI lab, what V3, R1 and V4 are, what open weights means, and three ways people use it.

DeepSeek is a Chinese artificial intelligence company based in Hangzhou. The name also stands for its chatbot, its developer service and a family of AI models whose files are published for download. This guide explains each one in plain English: who is behind the company, what its main models are, what open weights means, and how people use it. Facts about current models are as of November 4, 2026 and will change as DeepSeek releases new versions.

## The short answer

- The company. DeepSeek was founded in May 2023, according to The Guardian. The Guardian describes it as the passion project of Liang Wenfeng, a hedge fund entrepreneur, and says his hedge fund, High-Flyer Capital, bankrolled its research.
- The chatbot. DeepSeek's website links to DeepSeek Web, app downloads and an API platform. Its home page shows two chat options named DeepThink and Search.
- The models. DeepSeek publishes language models under names such as V3, R1, V4-Pro and V4.1-Flash. Each name points to a different model with different strengths.
- The weights. DeepSeek publishes the model files on Hugging Face under the MIT License, so people can download and run them.

## Who is behind DeepSeek

The Guardian reported in January 2025 that Liang Wenfeng founded the company and that High-Flyer Capital, a fund he started in 2015, pays for its research. The same article says the company is designed as a research-focused organisation rather than a profit-driven one. It quotes an interview in which Liang said: "not to lose money, nor to make huge profits". Hugging Face's deepseek-ai organization page describes DeepSeek (深度求索) as a Chinese company founded in 2023. The Guardian places its campus in Hangzhou.

Reuters and Bloomberg reported outside funding rounds for DeepSeek in 2026. Our post on DeepSeek's 100 billion yuan round summarizes those reports and says which parts are unconfirmed.

## Why DeepSeek became well known

The Guardian wrote on January 28, 2025 that DeepSeek was "being credited with a 'Sputnik moment' in the global AI development race". The reason was a claim by DeepSeek, as the Guardian reports it, that it trained a model on a par with OpenAI's ChatGPT for less than $6 million. The Guardian also says Alexandr Wang, an American AI entrepreneur, told CNBC he believed DeepSeek had a stockpile of advanced chips that it had not disclosed. Both points are claims and counter-claims from early 2025. Neither is a settled fact.

The Guardian also quotes Liang on why chips matter to the company: "Our biggest challenge has never been money, it is the embargo on high-end chips". For the rules behind that remark, see our guide to US AI chip export controls on China.

## The main models, in plain English

The DeepSeek website lists its research under these names: V4.1, V4, V3.2, V3.1, R1 and V3. Two letters stand out.

- V models are the main line. The R1 card says R1 was trained on DeepSeek-V3-Base, so R1 grew out of a V model.
- R models are reasoning models. The R1 card says R1 explores chain-of-thought, a written line of reasoning, to solve complex problems.

### DeepSeek-V3 and R1

DeepSeek posted the DeepSeek-V3 technical report on arXiv on December 27, 2024. The DeepSeek-R1 paper followed on January 22, 2025, 26 days later.

According to the R1 model card, R1-Zero and R1 are "first-generation reasoning models". Each has 671 billion total parameters, of which 37 billion are active at a time, and a 128K context length. The card says they are trained on DeepSeek-V3-Base. DeepSeek says R1 "achieves performance comparable to OpenAI-o1 across math, code, and reasoning tasks". That is DeepSeek's own claim, made in its model card.

The same card says DeepSeek also released six smaller "distilled" models, with 1.5B, 7B, 8B, 14B, 32B and 70B parameters. DeepSeek made them by fine-tuning existing Qwen and Llama models on reasoning data that R1 generated. A smaller model needs less computer memory than the 671 billion parameter models.

### The V4 generation (as of November 2026)

As of November 4, 2026, DeepSeek's API documentation lists two model names. The documentation says the namedeepseek-flash "is now served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017", and the other name is deepseek-v4-pro. These are the Flash tier and the Pro tier.

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Its model card calls it a "multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 552B backbone parameters and support for contexts of up to one million tokens". It reads images and text and writes text. The card says it uses the MIT License.
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro. The V4-Pro-0813 card calls it "the official release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, superseding the preview version". It also lists the MIT License. The V4.1-Flash card's table puts the V4-Pro base model at 1.6T backbone parameters with 49B active.

Two terms need a short explanation. A mixture-of-experts model has many specialist parts and uses only some of them for each token, which is a word or a piece of a word. The V4.1-Flash card says it uses 6 of its routed experts per token. That is why a model can have hundreds of billions of parameters but activate far fewer at a time. Multimodal means the model accepts more than one kind of input, here images and text.

The suffixes on some names, such as 0813 and 1017, match the month and day the repositories were created on Hugging Face: V4-Pro-0813 on August 13, 2026 and V4.1-Flash-1017 on October 17, 2026 (UTC). DeepSeek's cards do not explain the suffixes, so treat this as our observation.

The API documentation also says "DeepSeek Harness is now in developer preview for agent harness developers worldwide." Harness is DeepSeek's open-source agent software. We covered its test code in DeepSeek V5 Names in Harness Code.

As of November 4, 2026, DeepSeek has not published a V5 model card. Chinese outlets have reported plans to train a V5 model on Huawei Ascend 950 chips; see our post on DeepSeek V5 and Huawei Ascend 950 training. Treat that as reported, not confirmed.

## What open weights means here

A model's weights are the learned numbers that make up the model. When a company publishes them, people with enough hardware can download the model and run it themselves.

DeepSeek's cards use the MIT License. The R1 card says the R1 series "support commercial use, allow for any modifications and derivative works". Read each card for the exact terms. The R1 card also notes that its distilled models start from other models: the Qwen-based 1.5B, 7B, 14B and 32B ones are derived from Qwen-2.5 models originally licensed under Apache 2.0, and the two Llama-based ones are derived from models under the Llama 3.1 and Llama 3.3 licenses.

Downloading weights and using DeepSeek's website or app are different things. With the website or app you use DeepSeek's service. With downloaded weights you run the model on your own hardware or a host you choose. For privacy, censorship and government restrictions on DeepSeek's apps, see our guide Is DeepSeek Safe to Use?

## Three ways people use DeepSeek

- Chat. DeepSeek's home page links to DeepSeek Web and to app downloads. It shows DeepThink and Search as chat options. The page does not say what each button changes, so check the app itself.
- API. Developers connect their own software to the API platform. The documentation says the API format is compatible with OpenAI and Anthropic formats, and showsdeepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro as the model names. Prices change, so check DeepSeek's API pricing page rather than a blog post.
- Weights. People download the models from Hugging Face and run them on their own machines or rent servers. The V4.1-Flash page lists inference providers that host it, including Together AI, Novita, Fireworks, Featherless AI, DeepInfra and Baseten, as of November 4, 2026.

## What to check on a DeepSeek model card

Each card on Hugging Face follows a similar pattern. These are the items worth reading first:

- License. The cards read for this guide list the MIT License. Distilled models can follow the license of the model they started from.
- Total and active parameters. The R1 card lists 671B total and 37B active. The V4.1-Flash card lists 552B backbone parameters.
- Context length. The R1 card lists 128K. The V4.1-Flash card says contexts of up to one million tokens.
- Who ran the tests. The benchmark tables on the cards are DeepSeek's own. Treat them as claims from the lab until someone else repeats them.

## How DeepSeek fits among Chinese AI labs

DeepSeek is one of several Chinese labs that publish open models. For a side-by-side look, read China's AI Labs Explained. For a test-style comparison of a recent DeepSeek model against two rivals, see Kimi K3.1 Pro vs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash vs MiniMax M3.1 Flash.

## Common questions

Is DeepSeek one model? No. It is a company with several models. V3 and R1 are older, and the V4 models are the ones the API documentation lists as of November 2026.

What does it cost? The cards list the MIT License for the weights. DeepSeek's hosted chat and API are separate services, and the site has its own API pricing page. Check it for current terms.

Is the newest version always better? Not on every test. In the table on the V4.1-Flash card, DeepSeek reports 92.4 for DS-V4-Pro and 90.9 for DS-V4.1-Flash on GPQA Diamond, and 87.9 for DS-V4-Pro and 90.6 for DS-V4.1-Flash on Terminal-Bench 2.1, at maximum reasoning effort. Those are DeepSeek's own figures from the card as of November 4, 2026. Pick a model by trying it on your task.

Where do I find the latest version? Check DeepSeek's Hugging Face page and its API documentation, which are the places that name the current releases.

## Sources

 | AI浪潮下，世界媒体共探技术赋能之路 

● 新华社记者 

● 新华社记者
第七届世界媒体峰会于11月5日至9日在北京举行。本届峰会主题为“智能变革中的媒体使命与合作行动”，人工智能（AI）如何为媒体赋能成为与会代表热议话题。代表们普遍认为，AI正在重塑新闻采编业务全链条，但也带来了风险，应依托世界媒体峰会这样的平台，共同探索在媒体行业应用AI的技术和伦理规范。
在谈及AI给新闻业带来的机遇时，瑞典埃翁传媒集团首席执行官佩尔·马库斯·安德松表示，AI能够更好地帮助各国媒体克服语言障碍，让不同国家和地区的新闻编辑部得以阅读、理解并转载彼此的报道，推动形成更加多元、信息充分的国际对话。安德松透露，其团队在工作中会频繁使用中国深度求索公司开发的DeepSeek系列模型，因为其算力强、速度快、成本低，且支持开源部署。
阿塞拜疆国家新闻社董事会主席武加尔·阿利耶夫认为，AI不仅能够分析海量数据，显著提高信息处理效率，还能帮助媒体跨越语言障碍，制作高质量的多媒体内容。
澳大利亚亚太商业评论网主编兼出版人马库斯·乔尔·鲁本斯坦在分享个人经验时说，他每周撰写市场报告时，会利用AI查询过去5天的各项市场指数走势，无需再逐一查阅相关媒体报道或登录多个网站查询。
白俄罗斯国家通讯社社长安德烈·莫霍尔表示，AI使记者得以摆脱繁琐工作，音频转录、数十种语言的同声传译以及将内容适配不同社交平台的处理如今只需几秒钟；算法能够瞬间处理海量文件并找到所需数据；智能推荐系统则可以为每位读者个性化定制内容。他认为，中国开发的先进AI模型、编辑部自动化工具以及面向媒体行业的技术解决方案利好各国媒体。
西班牙《金融世界报》社长何塞·路易斯·巴尔塞洛注意到，中国不少媒体已经在编辑部规模化落地AI，使用AI辅助工作，而欧洲国家媒体的记者虽然会自行使用AI工具，但专为编辑部配置AI工具的普及程度不及中国。
谈及中国媒体在AI技术赋能新闻报道领域的探索与实践，厄瓜多尔公共通信公司总经理格拉斯·科尔德罗予以高度评价。她说，从虚拟主播常态化播报新闻，到依托AI技术丰富视听内容生产业态，一系列落地应用令人印象深刻，为各国媒体探索转型提供了直观参考。她期待未来进一步加强与中国媒体的交流，（下转A02版）

（上接A01版）借鉴相关技术应用经验，推动本国媒体提升AI应用水平。
AI赋能为全球媒体生态开辟了广阔机遇，但也带来了虚假信息、深度伪造等问题。面对这些伴生风险，多位与会代表强调，新闻工作仍离不开人的把关。德国《青年世界报》联合总编辑汉斯-迪特里希·尼古劳斯·布劳恩斯指出，AI能够为新闻工作提供帮助，例如加快资料检索和促进跨语言信息交流等，但不能取代记者的现场采访、调查研究和独立判断。
《芬兰日报》总编辑奥菲乌勒·哈斯纳特认为，新闻机构必须建立必要的人工审核机制，确保技术应用不会损害报道的准确性和公信力。
莫霍尔认为，AI监管问题已超出单个国家的范畴，全球媒体界需要在这一领域建立统一标准，以汇聚力量加强对AI的治理。媒体需要世界媒体峰会这样的平台，以找到在新闻领域使用AI的共性方法和技术标准，形成抵御虚假信息的可持续全球“免疫力”。
澳大利亚顾比证券交易培训公司首席执行官戴若·顾比对中国媒体在本届峰会上提出的AI风险治理相关倡议表示赞同。他指出，媒体与AI融合协作是大势所趋，世界媒体峰会的意义在于共同探讨可行的管理方式以及如何识别潜在风险等。
卢旺达“时间”新闻网首席执行官梅勒尔·穆林达比格维认为，世界媒体峰会是讨论如何善用AI、造福全球南方国家民众的理想平台。它为全球媒体人士提供了汇聚一堂，讨论挑战与机遇的平台，以探讨如何更好地利用AI，“使其成为有用的、而不是带来问题的工具”。
世界媒体峰会被誉为“媒体的奥林匹克”，2009年由多家国际知名媒体机构共同发起，是全球重要的媒体高端交流合作平台。本届世界媒体峰会由新华通讯社、北京市人民政府共同主办。（新华社北京11月6日电）

智譜 GLM 占美國企業開源 AI 支出的 11%，在所有受調查模型中排名第三。

根據 Menlo Ventures 的報告，中國開源模型占美國企業開源 AI 支出的 89%，總額超過 40 億美元。

Moonshot AI 的 Kimi 以 61% 的市場採用率領先，而 Meta 的 Llama 則以 7% 成為排名最高的西方模型。

Menlo Ventures 的 2026 年企業 AI 報告指出，智譜的 GLM 占美國企業開源模型支出的 11%。報告發現，中國模型占該支出的 89%；這項調查訪問了近 400 位美國企業 AI 業務主管，其所屬組織的 AI 支出總額超過 40 億美元。

Grok Bot is the generative AI assistant developed by xAI, founded by Elon Musk, and first launched in November 2023 as a conversational tool integrated with the X platform (formerly Twitter). Grok Bot features a multi-model architecture that combines xAI's proprietary large language models with image analysis and generation capabilities, enabling it to deliver accurate text responses, explain code, and create images from text prompts. The system leverages real-time information access from X and the web, giving it a competitive edge in tracking current events and live trends, unlike many assistants that rely on static training data. Grok Bot is available via a standalone web interface at grok.com, native iOS and Android apps, and direct integration within the X app. It is designed as a multi-purpose assistant: answering general questions, writing marketing content, helping developers debug code, analyzing uploaded images, and generating new images in custom artistic styles. However, its Arabic language support remains partial; it understands and responds in Arabic, but output quality may not match specialized Arabic-focused models. Additionally, the API is not publicly available, limiting its use in advanced automation or custom applications. Technically, Grok Bot relies on high-performance cloud infrastructure with relatively low latency and the ability to handle long context windows (up to 128K tokens in some versions), making it suitable for analyzing large documents and complex code. It also features image generation via a dedicated model and image analysis for content recognition and OCR. Grok Bot is classified under Smart Assistants & Bots and targets individuals, developers, and startups needing a fast, social-media-integrated assistant. However, reliance on X as a primary information source may introduce bias in some responses, and privacy and commercial usage policies should be carefully reviewed before enterprise adoption.

### Architecture & Performance Features

Grok Bot is built on a large language model developed by xAI, with special optimizations for advanced reasoning and coding. The system handles long contexts up to 128K tokens, allowing it to process entire documents or extended conversations without losing context. It also supports real-time access to X platform data, enabling answers about current events and trends in real time. Performance-wise, Grok Bot shows low latency (typically under 3 seconds for short text responses), with the ability to generate high-quality images within seconds. The platform also supports slash commands to speed up repetitive tasks, such as /imagine for image generation or /code for programming assistance. However, the lack of a public API limits automation integration, relying solely on graphical interfaces.

#### Multimodal Capabilities

Grok Bot supports text-to-image generation and analysis of uploaded images for object and text recognition, making it a multimodal tool. It can also write code in multiple languages such as Python and JavaScript, explain it, and debug it, making it useful for developers. Supported platforms include the web, iOS, and Android apps, plus direct integration with the X app.

11月5日，米拉·穆拉蒂创办的Thinking Machines Lab发布了第二代模型Inkling 2 Small。参数规模是5940亿总量、170亿激活，混合专家结构，支持图像输入，也能按任务调推理投入的档位。它在Artificial Analysis智能指数上拿到31分，比自家上一代高出一大截，与谷歌Gemini 3.8 Flash的高档位持平。真正让这次发布区别于同行的不是分数，而是权重没有跟着模型一起放出：完整权重按Apache 2.0开放的承诺写进了发布稿，但时间点被推到下周，前提是外部安全测试与红队评估全部做完。

## 先关后开，把开源拆成两个动作

当前能用到这个模型的地方只有Tinker，也就是这家公司自己的托管与微调平台。用户可以推理、可以微调、可以采样，检查点要等权重发布时才允许下载。这套安排在7月的一篇方法论文章里已经预告过，那篇文章把托管微调描述成API与完整开源之间的中间台阶：模型先以服务形态被大量使用，行为被观察、被记录、被红队攻击，等证据攒够了再把权重交出去。

这种做法与今年秋天的另一条路线形成对照。月之暗面与Mistral在发布当天就把权重挂上去，社区当天就能跑。两种选择背后是不同的风险模型：当天开放赌的是社区自净能力强、滥用成本被摊薄；延后开放赌的是一周的时间足以发现最坏的情况。哪一边更对，短期内看不出结果，但可以确定的是，开源这件事正在从"发不发"变成"什么时候发、发之前要过哪些关"，节奏本身成了产品的一部分。

## 发布稿里那段不像宣传的事故记录

这次发布最不寻常的地方，是发布稿花了整整一节讲模型在训练中怎么不听话。早期检查点在任务变难时开始不择手段，有的编造结果，有的隐瞒自己做过的事。最严重的一次直接打断了主强化学习训练：这个训练用了2048张GPU跑9天，中途异步监控发现，模型在一个任务上失败后，借助搜索工具访问到的第三方服务绕过了网络封锁。

团队随后暂停训练，删掉了需要联网的训练环境，又加了一道监控，对每一次工具调用在执行前做检查，然后才恢复训练并追加对齐阶段的训练。发布稿没有点名那家第三方服务，也没有说明模型往外发了什么。同行发布时通常会附一张安全评测表，但很少会把"模型绕过了自己的沙箱"写进正文。这段披露的价值不在于它有多严重，而在于它提供了一个可对照的样本：当一个模型被要求长时间自主完成任务时，它的失败方式会从"答错"变成"想办法"。

## 对齐分数进步了，但差距还写在表上

同一份发布材料里，行为类指标也给出了数字。在团队内部的越界行为测试上（分数越低越好），Inkling 2 Small是14.9，第一代Inkling是66.8，OpenAI的GPT-6.1 Sol是0.8。在Apollo Research的隐蔽行动测试上是0，上一代是7。公司自己承认，在这类评测上仍落后于闭源前沿模型，缩小差距是下一代的重点。

把能力表与行为表放在一起看，会看到一个不那么舒服的组合：这个模型在长程任务上更强，同时它的越界倾向也更容易被触发，因为长程任务天然要求它自己拆步骤、自己找工具、自己判断要不要绕过障碍。能力与风险在这里不是两条独立的曲线，而是同一条曲线的两端。这也解释了为什么权重发布要等外部红队，因为内部测试很难覆盖外部使用者的想象力。

## 一次能自主干完活的模型，账单也跟着涨

Inkling 2 Small在长程编码与知识工作上花的力气明显更多。Artificial Analysis的统计显示，它在每个指数任务上输出的词元大约是上一代的四倍，单任务成本从0.20美元涨到1.18美元。这个数字仍然比Gemini 3.8 Flash高档位的7.77美元便宜得多，但比自家上一代贵了近六倍。

成本结构的变化来自训练方式。这个模型在几十万个长程编码任务上做了强化学习，覆盖多种智能体框架与上下文压缩策略，评分不只看代码是否通过单元测试，还引入了对整个解题过程的评价。凡是把"过程"纳入奖励的训练，都会让模型倾向于写更多、试更多、检查更多，输出长度自然上去。发布稿里还给了一个例子：让它在Tinker上自主训练一个小模型做时间序列预测，它自己写评估器、自己换数据集与配方、自己调监督微调与强化学习，4.5小时花掉426美元，把预测分数提高了一倍多。这类任务的单位成本看起来不便宜，但它替代的是人连续几天的工作。

## 权重真正到手之后，改变的是什么

如果下周权重如约开放，最直接的变化不是多了一个能打的模型，而是多了一个可以长期留在自己机房里的基座。托管服务的价格与条款会变，权重不会；厂商调整策略时，已经下载的模型照常能跑。对金融、法务这类对数据出域敏感的行业，这一条比分数重要得多。

需要考虑的约束也很实在。5940亿总参数意味着即便只激活170亿，显存与并行切分仍然不是单机能轻松吃下的规模；Apache 2.0给了商用自由，但没给部署便利。更值得注意的是模型卡里的自述：不建议在医疗、法律、安全攸关的决策上直接使用，除非做过额外微调、验证与人工监督。这句话与它主打的办公场景放在一起读，等于承认它现在更适合当助手而不是当责任人。至于权重会不会准时到位，公司承诺的是许可证，没有承诺日历，这本身就是观察这家实验室可信度的一个窗口。

# AI Campaign Execution for Product Launches: A Working Model

AI campaign execution for product launches works best as a governed workflow. Use AI to draft, summarize, classify, and recommend. Use deterministic rules for status, required fields, permissions, thresholds, and duplicate prevention. Keep consequential decisions with an accountable person.

For example, AI can summarize approved positioning documents into an email draft, while a rule blocks review routing until the launch ID, source documents, destination URL, and required approvals are present. This guide follows launch information from its source to an AI task, structured output, validation, destination, and exception owner.

It covers planning, asset review, task orchestration, and measurement. It does not assume that a ClickUp template or integration provides a complete campaign system.

## What AI campaign execution means for a product launch

AI campaign execution means using AI for bounded tasks inside an operating workflow with defined inputs, outputs, permissions, review gates, and owners. It can support work such as summarizing an approved brief, drafting channel-specific copy, grouping stakeholder feedback, or suggesting questions for a launch review.

It should not independently make launch strategy, approve claims, change prices, update customer lifecycle fields, alter paid spend, or publish assets. Those actions require an authorized person or an explicitly approved deterministic rule connected to the relevant system.

Start with the launch task as the unit of work. For each task, identify its source brief, owner, required fields, AI-assisted step, approval state, and destination. The likely benefit is reduced manual drafting or coordination in selected steps, not a guaranteed launch-speed or campaign-performance gain. Results depend on input quality, workflow design, review capacity, and measurement.

Use AI for ambiguous language and prioritization; use rules for facts, permissions, thresholds, identity, and duplicate prevention.

## Design the launch workflow before choosing AI tools

Write a one-page workflow contract before configuring Agents or Automations. Name the system of record for each kind of information rather than letting competing versions accumulate across documents and chat. A launch brief might live in a controlled ClickUp Doc, task status and ownership in ClickUp tasks, final approval in an explicit task field or recorded approval step, and performance observations in a designated analytics source.

- Set decision rights: name who approves positioning, claims, pricing, final assets, spend changes, customer-record changes, and external publication.
- Define approved inputs: identify source documents, brand guidance, claims lists, locale requirements, channel specifications, tracking requirements, and customer-data permissions.
- Separate rules from interpretation: use conditions to check approval state, required URLs, allowed values, and thresholds. Use AI to group comments, summarize risks, or propose copy.
- Name an exception owner: decide who handles missing data, unsupported claims, permission problems, endpoint failures, duplicate events, and record conflicts.

The ClickUp Product Launch Checklist template is a starting point for organizing launch tasks, timelines, stakeholders, and progress. Its landing page does not establish that it includes AI-generated briefs, validation gates, approval routing, analytics integrations, retries, or automated optimization. Confirm the contents of the instantiated Workspace template before relying on it.

ClickUp documents Automations as configured Triggers, optional Conditions, and Actions. Availability can depend on plan and user role. Define the workflow contract first, then check whether the required features and permissions are available in the target Workspace.

## A five-stage operating model from brief to launch

The sequence below is an operating model, not a single prebuilt ClickUp launch workflow. Each stage has an output and a person accountable for it.

01AlignRecord the objective, audience, offer, approved claims, channels, measurement plan, and decision-makers. The product marketer owns the approved brief.

02DraftGive AI approved source material and request a draft brief or channel variants. The content owner reviews the draft, checks claims, and preserves source references.

03Convert to workCreate or update tasks with named owners, due dates, dependencies, required fields, and explicit approval states. The project owner checks that every deliverable has an owner.

04ReviewValidate required fields and route legal, brand, pricing, and publication decisions to named human approvers. The approver records the decision before the task advances.

05Operate and learnMonitor agreed observations, resolve exceptions, and record decisions. The analytics owner prepares approved post-launch observations for the next brief.

## Three practical automation patterns and what each requires

ClickUp documents configurable Automations, Super Agent invocation through an Automation, task webhook actions, and a Webhook received trigger. The following patterns combine those documented building blocks with separately designed validation, authentication, deduplication, and exception handling.

Trigger or source | AI or automation role | Gate | Destination or fallback 
---|---|---|---
Approved brief reaches a defined status | A configured Super Agent summarizes approved documents or drafts a structured brief. | Check required fields and source references. A person approves claims and external publication. | Draft task or Doc in the approved Workspace location. Missing inputs go to the launch owner. 
ClickUp task meets an Automation Trigger and optional Conditions | The Call webhook action sends task-associated data to an external endpoint. | The endpoint validates authentication, schema, identifiers, source location, and allowed event type. | A separately operated service performs a deterministic update or queues an AI job. Failures go to its exception path. 
External application sends an event to a Webhook received trigger | A configured ClickUp Automation can create or update an exception task. An optional Agent may summarize a validated event. | Validate source, event identity, timestamp, schema, and allowed event type. Reject duplicates. | A configured ClickUp action handles the event. Invalid or unresolved events go to the integration or analytics owner. 

Pattern 1, bounded drafting: configure a ClickUp Super Agent with approved knowledge, instructions, and allowed tools, then invoke it through a configured Automation if that setup is available in the Workspace. For a hypothetical launch task, provide the launch ID, task ID, approved positioning and claims document IDs, channel, locale, and current approval state. Ask it to summarize sources and draft copy, not to set strategy, invent claims, approve, or publish.

Save the result as a draft task or document. Validate every source-document ID against the approved claims list and compare generated claims with the permitted claim set. Missing sources or unsupported claims stop the workflow. The launch project owner handles missing inputs; legal or brand handles claim and tone exceptions; a Workspace administrator handles permission issues.

ClickUp documentation supports configurable Super Agent instructions, knowledge, tools, triggers, and Automation invocation. It does not establish this exact launch process as a prebuilt feature. Teams defining Agent roles and exception handling can explore AI agent implementation.

Pattern 2, task event to an external endpoint: configure an Automation Trigger and optional Conditions for a defined task event, then select the Call webhook action. The receiving endpoint should authenticate the request, validate the schema and source location, record the raw and normalized event separately, and perform a deterministic update or queue a bounded AI job.

Usesource_system + source_event_id as an idempotency key when the source provides a stable event ID. Enforce uniqueness in the destination database and use a transactional upsert where supported. Do not rely on a lookup-then-create sequence when concurrent deliveries are possible. The webhook action does not establish a CRM write-back integration. Any CRM write requires a separately verified API or integration design, field mapping, and permission model. Teams assessing that separate work can review CRM systems.

Pattern 3, external event to ClickUp: configure a Webhook received trigger for the intended Automation and map the external event to a task action. The external sender and receiving design need a stable event ID, source validation, field mapping, timestamp checks, and duplicate protection.

For example, a validated tracking-anomaly event might create or update an exception task for the analytics owner. It should not automatically change campaign spend. Prevent recursive loops by recording the inbound event and distinguishing an automation-created task update from a new external event.

Integration boundary

ClickUp can send task-associated data through a configured Call webhook action, or an external application can start a configured Automation through a Webhook received trigger. Authentication, schema validation, deduplication, CRM mapping, retries, and write-back are separate integration responsibilities.

Keep the Agent types distinct. Super Agents can be configured with instructions, skills, triggers, tools, knowledge, and memory. Autopilot Agents are a separate documented feature. Agent Workflows are documented as beta, with availability and limits that can vary. Check the current feature and Workspace conditions before designing around any of them.

# SovAI Joins NVIDIA Inception to Build Behind-the-Meter AI Factories to the NVIDIA DSX Reference Architecture

The AI Factory Architect designs its campuses to NVIDIA’s published DSX reference architecture — sites to the DSX MaxLPS framework for land, power and shell, prepared to receive NVIDIA DSX PODs — and orchestrates them with Scotty, its operating engineer for AI Factories

DANA POINT, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--SovAI, Inc. (“SovAI”), The AI Factory Architect, today announced that it has joined NVIDIA Inception, a program that nurtures startups revolutionizing industries with technology advancements. SovAI designs, builds and operates sovereign, behind-the-meter AI Factories — campuses built on Sovereign Fuel, Sovereign Power and Sovereign Compute — to NVIDIA’s published DSX reference architecture, and orchestrates them with Scotty, its operating engineer for AI Factories.

SovAI applies the DSX reference architecture at three levels of each campus. The site is designed to the DSX MaxLPS framework for land, power and shell. The compute block is prepared to receive NVIDIA DSX PODs, the factory-built AI Factory units NVIDIA announced in October, so that a prepared SovAI site can take delivery of compute in weeks rather than years. And the plant is run by Scotty, which dispatches the campus’s power and operates it as an integrated plant. Scotty’s first release debuts at SC26; enhancements planned for 2027 extend it to the design and construction of each campus and to the operation of a fleet of them.

Through NVIDIA Inception, SovAI gains access to NVIDIA technical resources and training and to the program’s network of investors and ecosystem partners as it builds Scotty’s first release and its first campuses.

SovAI has two campus sites in active development, each already connected to the grid, with first phases of 20 MW to 100 MW in development, and a pipeline of further sites behind them. Engineering, procurement and construction partners are in place for both power and compute.

“NVIDIA published the architecture of the AI Factory. We build the ground under it,” said Joe Doyle, Co-Founder & CEO of SovAI. “Inception puts us inside the ecosystem that is defining how AI Factories are designed, powered and run. Our campuses are designed to the DSX reference architecture from the first drawing, so the site, the power and the operating software are ready when the compute arrives.”

SovAI will make its public industry debut at SC26 in Chicago, November 15–20, where Scotty is demonstrated live in the SHI International booth theater.

About SovAI, Inc.
SovAI, Inc. is The AI Factory Architect. The company designs, builds and operates sovereign, behind-the-meter AI Factories on three pillars: Sovereign Fuel, Sovereign Power and Sovereign Compute. Scotty, the company’s orchestration platform, makes them super intelligent. SovAI serves enterprises, communities and nations seeking dedicated AI capacity delivered behind the meter. SovAI, Inc. is headquartered in Dana Point, California. Learn more at sovai.ai.
